prompt: A support organization wants a reusable, reviewed refund-triage Skill only for its support team. Engineering should not inherit it, and the owner needs to update or revoke it later. The organization’s supported distribution platform provides group-targeted plugins with versioned updates and removal. What distribution plan best fits?

options.text: Install for everyone and ask engineering to ignore it.
Assign an owned, versioned plugin only to the support group.
Paste separate prompt copies instead of managing releases.
Distribute the instructions inside a shared MCP credential.

feedback.reason: Bundle the reviewed Skill in the supported group-targeted plugin and assign it only to support. The owner controls its reviewed updates and removal through that distribution path.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A Skill is a reusable instruction/workflow asset; its delivery and scope are separate from credentials and live tool authorization.
details.scenarioApplication: Bundle the reviewed Skill in the supported group-targeted plugin and assign it only to support. The owner controls its reviewed updates and removal through that distribution path.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Verify the supported distribution and update behavior in the target product; a Skill does not itself grant tool access or guarantee policy enforcement.
details.errorCorrection: Separate audience, release ownership, effective installation state, and permission enforcement.
details.transfer: Treat reusable assets as owned releases with audience, version, and removal paths.

messages.text: Installing for everyone violates the stated support-only audience; a README does not restrict availability.
Manual prompt copies lose the reviewed version and controlled update or removal path.
Credentials authenticate access; they are not a distribution mechanism for reusable instructions.

prompt: A company has a centrally owned security-review Skill that should be available across repositories and updated by a single owner. It is guidance, not a technical access-control boundary. Teams also have repository-specific build guidance. How should those assets be organized?

options.text: Let each repository edit its own central security copy.
Put all guidance in an ownerless global file.
Govern the shared Skill centrally; keep project guidance local.
Let each user maintain an independently edited central Skill copy.

feedback.reason: The intended audience and change authority differ: centrally governed common guidance and project-local instructions need separate ownership/scopes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Scope should match who needs the asset and who controls its lifecycle.
details.scenarioApplication: The intended audience and change authority differ: centrally governed common guidance and project-local instructions need separate ownership/scopes.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Verify the supported distribution and update behavior in the target product; a Skill does not itself grant tool access or guarantee policy enforcement.
details.errorCorrection: Separate audience, release ownership, effective installation state, and permission enforcement.
details.transfer: Separate shared baseline assets from project-specific customization.

messages.text: Independent edits to central guidance defeat single-owner updates and create divergent copies.
An ownerless global file does not distinguish central governance from project-specific responsibility.
Independently edited user copies fragment the centrally owned asset and its update path; optional invocation is a different question from release ownership.

prompt: A reviewed Skill was installed across a team, but its instructions now conflict with a changed workflow. The previous version remains in several developer environments. What is the strongest lifecycle response?

options.text: Edit source and assume every installation updates immediately.
Keep all obsolete copies active with a staleness warning.
Delete source and let users choose any remaining local copy.
Release and verify the update; remove obsolete active versions.

feedback.reason: A source edit does not establish that distributed copies were replaced; version and revocation behavior must be managed and checked.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Reusable assets can become operationally stale, so release state and deployed state need a traceable relationship.
details.scenarioApplication: A source edit does not establish that distributed copies were replaced; version and revocation behavior must be managed and checked.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Verify the supported distribution and update behavior in the target product; a Skill does not itself grant tool access or guarantee policy enforcement.
details.errorCorrection: Separate audience, release ownership, effective installation state, and permission enforcement.
details.transfer: Close the loop between asset authorship, distribution, update, and removal.

messages.text: Editing source does not show which versions existing environments actually use.
A warning does not prevent obsolete instructions from remaining active.
Deleting source does not remove already distributed local copies or provide a supported update path.

prompt: A Skill containing internal procedures is being considered for a public community repository. It has no secrets, but the intended audience is currently only the company’s support staff. What should its owner do?

options.text: Keep distribution internal until public release is approved.
Publish now because no credentials means no disclosure risk.
Let employees publish internal procedures from personal scope.
Convert it to a prompt to remove distribution governance.

feedback.reason: No secrets does not mean that internal process knowledge is intended for public release; distribution scope is part of governance.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Audience and ownership decisions apply to reusable instructions as well as executable code.
details.scenarioApplication: No secrets does not mean that internal process knowledge is intended for public release; distribution scope is part of governance.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Verify the supported distribution and update behavior in the target product; a Skill does not itself grant tool access or guarantee policy enforcement.
details.errorCorrection: Separate audience, release ownership, effective installation state, and permission enforcement.
details.transfer: Match distribution scope to the approved audience and lifecycle.

messages.text: Internal procedure knowledge can require disclosure approval even when it contains no credentials.
Personal scope does not authorize employees to publish company procedures.
Rewriting a procedure as a prompt does not remove its audience or disclosure restrictions.

prompt: A coding convention is needed only in one Claude Code repository. The team wants the Skill version to travel with reviewed repository changes and be restorable through repository history. Which approach fits?

options.text: Commit the project Skill in .claude/skills with the repository.
Keep separate personal copies and reconcile them only after failures.
Upload it to every organization member regardless of project scope.
Store it in a shared token so authentication controls its version.

feedback.reason: A repository-scoped Skill can version with the repository and use its reviewed history for rollback. Verify that users run the intended revision and refresh the relevant session state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A repository-scoped Skill can version with the repository and use its reviewed history for rollback. Verify that users run the intended revision and refresh the relevant session state.
details.scenarioApplication: A repository-scoped Skill can version with the repository and use its reviewed history for rollback. Verify that users run the intended revision and refresh the relevant session state.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Repository rollback changes the tracked artifact; it is not proof every running session has adopted it.
details.errorCorrection: Check the artifact actually selected or installed, not just its documentation.
details.transfer: Connect release ownership and version history to observed behavior in the target environment.

messages.text: Independent personal copies do not establish one reviewed repository version.
Organization-wide distribution exceeds the stated single-repository audience.
A token is an authentication secret, not versioned procedure content.

prompt: A product invokes a custom Skill programmatically through an API that supports selecting an explicit Skill version. The tested release must remain stable while a newer version is evaluated. What should the calling system do?

options.text: Select latest on every call and assume updates preserve behavior.
Pin the tested version; evaluate and deliberately switch releases.
Use an organization chat upload as proof of the API’s active version.
Change only the README and assume all API callers follow it.

feedback.reason: Use the supported explicit version in the API caller, evaluate the candidate against the product contract, and switch or roll back through an owned release decision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Use the supported explicit version in the API caller, evaluate the candidate against the product contract, and switch or roll back through an owned release decision.
details.scenarioApplication: Use the supported explicit version in the API caller, evaluate the candidate against the product contract, and switch or roll back through an owned release decision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Pinning controls artifact selection, not model determinism or the permissions of tools the Skill uses.
details.errorCorrection: Check the artifact actually selected or installed, not just its documentation.
details.transfer: Connect release ownership and version history to observed behavior in the target environment.

messages.text: Latest can change the invoked artifact before its behavior is evaluated for this product.
Chat availability does not establish the version selected by a separate programmatic caller.
Documentation alone does not change the caller’s actual version selection.

prompt: A governed team Skill update changes an output format and breaks a downstream parser. The distribution system has a tested rollback path to the previous approved version. What should its owner verify during recovery?

options.text: Only that the source repository now contains the old text.
Verify the effective version and restored parser compatibility.
That a README warning exists while the broken release remains active.
That all historical outputs can be relabeled as correctly formatted.

feedback.reason: Use the tested rollback, verify the effective version in affected environments, and check parser compatibility. A source change alone does not show recovery of distributed execution.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Use the tested rollback, verify the effective version in affected environments, and check parser compatibility. A source change alone does not show recovery of distributed execution.
details.scenarioApplication: Use the tested rollback, verify the effective version in affected environments, and check parser compatibility. A source change alone does not show recovery of distributed execution.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Handle already produced bad outputs separately; restoring a version does not undo their downstream effects.
details.errorCorrection: Check the artifact actually selected or installed, not just its documentation.
details.transfer: Connect release ownership and version history to observed behavior in the target environment.

messages.text: Source state does not establish the version used by installations or active sessions.
A warning leaves the observed incompatibility in place.
Relabeling cannot repair invalid historical output or prove current compatibility.
